comparator.name: Biomedical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum totals 180 EC. Years 1 and 2 are each complete 60-EC compulsory sequences integrating mathematics, physics, engineering design, life science, imaging, computation and ethics. The selected 30-EC year-three deepening minor follows the first-listed Biomaterials Science and Engineering package through one main and two other courses in each period. The final semester contains 15 EC of compulsory and restricted-choice work plus a 15-EC bachelor project.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target names no year-three specialisation. The official programme presents Biomaterials Science and Engineering, Medical Device Design and Medical Imaging as parallel options without identifying a general route. Biomaterials Science and Engineering appears first and is selected independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Biomedical technology, computation & design
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule visibly combines life science, anatomy, quantitative methods, biomedical data, imaging, product design, robotics, ethics and disease applications.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines biomedical foundations with mathematics, programming, image analysis, machine learning, signal systems, product design and robotics for healthcare technology.
progression: Biomedical, programming, data and mathematical foundations precede molecular biology, anatomy, physiology, imaging, machine learning, product design, disease study, signal systems and robotics. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Medical-device design, robotics & innovation
alternatives.labelReason: Product design, robotics, biomedical science, marketing, regulation, governance, strategy and negotiation form a device-development route.
alternatives.concept: A medical-device route combining biomedical knowledge, user-centred product design, image analysis and robotics with entrepreneurship, marketing, regulation, governance, strategy and responsible innovation.
progression: Biomedical, programming, mathematics, enterprise and research foundations precede product design, imaging, machine learning, device governance, robotics, marketing and strategic negotiation. All prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces much of the closest programme’s advanced mathematics, signals, immunology and quantitative biomedical depth with product design, enterprise, regulation, marketing and strategic implementation. It differs by more than 30 EC.

alternatives.label: Medical imaging, modelling & biomedical data
alternatives.labelReason: Image processing, neural networks, signals, optimisation, numerical modelling, databases and biomedical science form a clear imaging-and-data route.
alternatives.concept: A medical-imaging and biomedical-data route combining anatomy, physiology and molecular biology with programming, image processing, machine learning, neural networks, signals, numerical methods, databases and optimisation.
progression: Programming, mathematical, life-science, neurobiology and statistical foundations precede anatomy, image processing, numerical methods, machine learning, neural networks, signals, databases and optimisation. All prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route centres image formation, computation and quantitative biomedical modelling rather than product commercialisation or the broad biomedical-technology mix. It clears the 30-EC floor against both earlier programmes.

core: Biomedical life science, anatomy, physiology and disease

questions: How can engineering and computation improve diagnosis and therapy?
How can devices, prosthetics and artificial organs restore or monitor body functions?
How can healthcare technology support prevention, sustainability and responsible innovation?

selection.assessment: A defensible closest UCR response combines biomedical science, computation, imaging, design and robotics while recording the missing physics and materials sequence. Medical-device innovation and medical imaging/data are separately evidenced, coherent, mechanically feasible and pairwise distinct. A biomaterials route was assessed but rejected as infeasible; production stops at the maximum of three included alternatives.

notes.text: Groningen Biomedical Engineering combines sustained physics, mechanics, electronics, materials science, biomaterials, laboratories and engineering design. UCR can combine biomedical science, mathematics, data, imaging, robotics, product design and innovation, but these are related liberal-arts pathways rather than a full accredited biomedical-engineering sequence.
